title: CANDID: Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution in Local Computer-Use Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.24977v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We present CANDID (Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution), an execution-control framework designed to enhance the reliability of local computer-use agents (CUAs) in resource-constrained settings. While local CUAs feature robust baseline proficiency in single-step action prediction, they frequently fail at critical junctions due to rigid action loops or premature DONE decisions. Rather than imposing imprecise cognitive loads through textual reflection, CANDID repurposes parallel test-time scaling into a disciplined, execution-level intervention at sparse, failure-prone points. We introduce a loop-recovery mechanism to filter candidates away from repeated behaviors and a conservative, unanimous DONE gating policy that requires absolute consensus to terminate. translated_title: CANDID：面向本地计算机使用代理规范执行的候选驱动干预框架
translated_abstract: 我们提出了CANDID（Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution，候选驱动干预的规范执行），这是一个执行控制框架，旨在提高本地计算机使用代理（CUA）在资源受限环境中的可靠性。虽然本地CUA在单步动作预测方面具备强大的基线能力，但它们经常在关键节点因僵化的动作循环或过早的DONE决策而失败。CANDID并未通过文本反思施加不精确的认知负担，而是将并行测试时扩展重新用于在稀疏的、易失败的节点上实施规范化的执行级干预。我们引入了一种循环恢复机制来过滤掉重复行为的候选方案，以及一种保守的、要求全体一致的DONE门控策略，即必须达成绝对共识才能终止任务。在OSWorld上的实验表明，CANDID的结构化控制显著提高了成功率，以极小的额外开销超越了基于反馈的替代方案。
tldr: CANDID是一个执行控制框架，通过循环恢复机制和全体一致的DONE门控策略，在易失败的关键节点对本地计算机使用代理实施规范化的执行级干预，显著提升了资源受限环境下的任务成功率。
en_tdlr: CANDID is an execution-control framework that applies disciplined, execution-level interventions at failure-prone points in local computer-use agents, using a loop-recovery mechanism and a unanimous DONE gating policy to significantly improve task success rates in resource-constrained settings.
